title: Support Automation: Unified Admin Catalog & Task Runner
creator: Rohit Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a single searchable catalog of admin utilities and runbooks where each runbook is represented as a first-class task (runnable via Console, API, or CLI) and backed by safe execution policies. This work unifies a grab-bag of scripts, interactive shells, and ad-hoc runbooks into a typed, permissioned task surface that support engineers and oncall can invoke quickly.

Scope:
- Build a metadata registry for runbooks (tags, inputs, outputs, estimated duration, RBAC requirements, audit annotations).
- Implement a lightweight task runner (runworklet) that accepts typed params, performs dry-run checks, and emits structured telemetry.
- Add Console UI hooks: quick-run, parameter presets, historical runs, and one-click rollback where applicable.
- Integrate with existing telemetry (Datadog dashboard + traces) and the incident timeline so runs are correlated with incidents.
- Safety: input validation, credential scoping (credentialed steps must use ephemeral privileged session), preflight canary and circuit-breaker policies.

Trade-offs discussed:
- We favor typed inputs + strict validation over freeform scripts to reduce blast radius, which increases upfront engineering work for wrapping legacy scripts.
- Live-preview/dry-run adds latency to the first execution but dramatically reduces error rate; decided to make dry-run optional but recommended for high-risk steps.
- We will not attempt to fully auto-convert all legacy runbooks in first iteration; prioritization will be by run frequency and incident impact.

Success metrics:
- 40% reduction in time-to-remediate for the 10 most common incident classes within 8 weeks of rollout.
- 80% of runbook executions include structured telemetry and outcome tags.
- No high-severity security findings during initial security review.

Deliverables:
- Metadata registry service + small schema and migration for existing runbooks.
- Runworklet runner service with API + CLI.
- Console quick-run surface and history panel.
- Migrations/wrappers for top 15 runbooks.

Notes: Link to design sketch and API contract in Confluence and the spike PR in GitHub (see links).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entries can be created/edited with tags, RBAC fields, and typed inputs
Runworklet can execute a dry-run and a real run; both produce consistent telemetry events
Console shows run history and allows re-run with parameter presets
Audit records capture invoker identity, inputs, and outcome for every run
implementation_notes: Phase 1: scaffold registry and typed schema; provide migration script for 5 high-priority runbooks
Phase 2: implement runner with ephemeral credential proxy + dry-run; integrate Datadog spans and metric tags
Phase 3: Console wiring, RBAC enforcement, rollout to oncall group via feature flag
